note_on_method: Each venue page rests on the City of Tallahassee's pickleball page, which gives one entry per outdoor venue with an address, a count line in the City's words and a weekly grid of Open Play, Reserved Play and First-Come First-Play, followed by the City's definitions of the three and its price table. Where the venue is a community centre, the centre's own page supplies building hours and a second copy of the address. The US Census address geocoder supplies the county and the postcode, which the City does not print. Where the City is silent, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
Six outdoor pickleball courts, and the six is the City's own arithmetic on one line: "2 courts with adjustable net straps, 4 courts with portable nets if needed and all have painted lines". Two courts carry a net permanently. Four more are painted for pickleball and take a portable net when one is wanted, and the City does not say who brings it.

This is the City's beginner venue on its own schedule. Open Play here is labelled "Beginner & Adv. Beginner Open Play" on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday mornings, with "Intermed. Open Play" on Saturday afternoons, and the City's Wednesday morning clinics are held here too.
slots.getting_there:
450 West 4th Avenue, Tallahassee, FL 32303. The US Census address geocoder matched "450 W 4TH AVE, TALLAHASSEE, FL, 32303" at house-number level, in Leon County inside the incorporated place Tallahassee city. The City prints no postcode for this venue, so the 32303 is the resolver's.

The City publishes nothing about parking here and nothing about restrooms. The phone number on the pickleball page is 850-891-3930.
slots.what_to_expect:
A rotation on three mornings a week and one afternoon, free. Open Play runs Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday 8:00am-12:00pm for beginners and advanced beginners, and Saturday 2:00pm-5:00pm for intermediates, and the City prices it at nothing: "all Open Play sessions are drop-in and free". Inside a session the "RACK" sets the order, games go to 11 and win by 2, or to 9 with all four players off when six are waiting.

Monday, Wednesday and Friday are first come, first play only, with a 90 minute limit when others are waiting and no price stated. No Reserved Play is scheduled here at all. Lighting is not stated, so evening play is an open question rather than a yes. Surface is not stated.

faqs.a: During Open Play, yes: the City writes that "all Open Play sessions are drop-in and free". First-come play outside sessions carries no stated price.
Yes. The City's clinics run here on Wednesday mornings: beginner 8:30-9:30, advanced beginner 9:30-10:30, intermediate 10:30-11:30, in sessions of four to eight weeks with online registration.

slots.description:
Twelve outdoor pickleball courts, the largest published set in Tallahassee, in two kinds the City counts on one line: "4 pickleball courts | 8 pickleball courts on multi-purpose courts (tennis courts 1-4)". Four stand alone as pickleball courts. Eight are lined onto tennis courts 1 to 4.

The City adds a sentence about who gets which: "City of Tallahassee pickleball professionals have priority to use courts 1A/1B for teaching purposes during non-monitored hours. Open Play schedule includes combo courts 4A-4B and the four standalone pickleball courts." On that numbering an Open Play session is six courts, the four standalone plus the pair on tennis court 4, rather than all twelve.
slots.getting_there:
501 Easterwood Avenue, Tallahassee, FL 32311, as the City writes it. The US Census address geocoder answered "501 EASTERWOOD DR, TALLAHASSEE, FL, 32311", the same number and the same postcode with the street type changed from Avenue to Drive, and OpenStreetMap holds no record of the address as the City writes it. There is one street here under one name, in Leon County inside Tallahassee city. The City prints no postcode; the 32311 is the resolver's.

The City publishes nothing about parking at the park.
slots.what_to_expect:
The fullest timetable in Tallahassee. Open Play, free and drop-in, runs Monday and Wednesday 8:00am-12:00pm and Sunday 8:00am-12:00pm and 5:00pm-8:30pm. Reserved Play, booked and paid at $3.50 to $5.75 a session, fills Monday to Thursday 5:30pm-8:30pm and Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday 8:30am-1:00pm. Friday is first come, first play only, and so is every hour not on the grid, with a 90 minute limit when others are waiting.

So: turn up on a Monday, Wednesday or Sunday morning and a rotation under the City's "RACK" rules will be there. Book and pay for a weekday evening. Bring your own game on a Friday. Whether the evening sessions are lit is not stated, and lighting is not inferred here from an 8:30pm finish. Surface is not stated. Two courts, 1A and 1B, belong to the City's coaches when nobody is monitoring.

faqs.a: During Open Play, yes, on Monday and Wednesday mornings and Sunday morning and evening. Reserved Play sessions cost $5.75 singles and $4.25 doubles, with senior rates of $4.75 and $3.50.
Online through Court Reserve, or by phone on 850-891-4940 between 9:00am and 10:00pm on weekdays and to 6:00pm at weekends. Only Reserved Play sessions can be booked.

slots.description:
Six outdoor courts that the City describes as shared rather than dedicated: "Winthrop Park tennis courts are multi-purpose courts used for tennis, pickleball and any other sports that will not damage the surface or nets of the courts". The count line is "6 courts", and nothing here is called a pickleball court in its own right.

Winthrop is the one published venue in Tallahassee with no Open Play session at all. Its grid is Reserved Play Monday to Thursday 5:30pm-8:30pm and Saturday 8:30am-1:00pm, with first come, first play at every other hour, Sunday included. It is one of the three venues the City takes online reservations for.
slots.getting_there:
1601 Mitchell Avenue, Tallahassee, FL 32303. The US Census address geocoder matched "1601 MITCHELL AVE, TALLAHASSEE, FL, 32303" at house-number level, in Leon County inside the incorporated place Tallahassee city. The City prints no postcode; the 32303 is the resolver's.

The City publishes nothing about parking or restrooms at this park and gives it no phone number of its own. The reservation line, 850-891-4940, is the published contact.
slots.what_to_expect:
Six courts you may have to share, and no fee answer. The City schedules no Open Play here, so no free session is stated, and it prices nothing for first come play, so no price is stated either. Reserved Play costs the City's table rate of $3.50 to $5.75 a session on the four weekday evenings and the Saturday morning it is offered.

The practical warnings are the City's own: "Please be aware that the GA/FL A and B league will be utilizing 5 courts on Tuesdays and 6 courts on Thursdays from 9:00am-12:00pm (September through April). In addition, local school teams will be using the courts from 3:30-5:00pm (January through April)." The City does not say which sport either plays, so a first come game on a spring weekday may find nowhere to play. The courts are tennis courts that take pickleball, and the City does not say whether pickleball nets are set or brought. Lighting is not stated and surface is not stated.

faqs.a: Not stated. No Open Play is scheduled here, and first-come play carries no price, so no fee answer is published. Reserved Play costs $3.50 to $5.75 a session.
Reserved Play runs Monday to Thursday 5:30pm-8:30pm and Saturday 8:30am-1:00pm, booked online through Court Reserve or on 850-891-4940. Friday is first come, first play only.

slots.description:
Two outdoor pickleball courts with their own nets, "2 courts with adjustable net straps and painted lines", at a community centre in a 52-acre park. They are first come, first play only, with no session of any kind on the City's grid.

The line to read first is the one under it: "Due to scheduled resurfacing, both the outdoor tennis and pickleball courts at jack mclean will be unavailable for  use until december 5, 2025." That date had passed by nine months when the page was read on 7 September 2026, and the notice was still there.

The centre's own page describes the park around the courts: five covered picnic shelters with grills, two comfort stations, a playground, four basketball courts, two tennis courts, two bike trails and a 24-hole disc golf course. The centre is open Monday to Saturday 9:00am to 9:00pm.
slots.getting_there:
700 Paul Russell Road, Tallahassee, FL 32301. The City prints the address twice, on the pickleball page and on the centre's own page, and they agree. The US Census address geocoder matched "700 PAUL RUSSELL RD, TALLAHASSEE, FL, 32301" at house-number level in Leon County inside Tallahassee city, and the centre page adds the postcode the pickleball page leaves off.

The City says nothing about parking. The centre's phone number is 850-891-2505.
slots.what_to_expect:
Nothing, on the City's page, until the resurfacing notice comes down, and the City has not said whether the courts have reopened. Ring 850-891-2505 before going. If they are open, they are first come, first play at all hours with a 90 minute limit when others are waiting, and no price is stated, so no fee answer is published. The nets are there: adjustable net straps and painted lines are the City's own description.

Lighting is not stated and surface is not stated, though a court being resurfaced is, in its way, the City's one remark about surface in Tallahassee. Two courts is a single game each: a four can play, an eight will wait.

faqs.a: The City's page still says they are unavailable for resurfacing "until december 5, 2025", a date nine months past when read on 7 September 2026. Ring 850-891-2505 before going.
The centre is on the City's indoor schedule with Open Play on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday, but the City states no indoor count, so nothing indoor is published.

slots.description:
Three courts in two places, in the City's own split: "1 indoor court, 2 outdoor courts". It is the one published Tallahassee venue with a court under a roof. The outdoor pair is first come, first play with hours stated, the only outdoor hours line the City gives anywhere in the city: "Outdoor FCFP: 8:00am - 9:00pm Daily, Closed on Sunday", printed here as the City prints it, "Daily" and "Closed on Sunday" together.

The indoor court appears on the City's indoor schedule for one window a week, Friday 12:00pm-2:00pm, labelled "Rerseve Play Only" in the City's spelling. The City states that "Indoor courts do not have First-Come First-Play available", so it is not somewhere to turn up.
slots.getting_there:
801 Bragg Drive, Tallahassee, FL 32305. The US Census address geocoder matched "801 BRAGG DR, TALLAHASSEE, FL, 32305" at house-number level, in Leon County inside the incorporated place Tallahassee city. The City prints no postcode; the 32305 is the resolver's.

The City publishes nothing about parking or restrooms here. The Friday indoor session is booked through the centre on 850-891-3940: the online system covers Four Oaks, Tom Brown and Winthrop, and "For all other locations that have Reserved Play sessions, please contact that facility directly."
slots.what_to_expect:
Outdoors, two first come courts from 8:00am to 9:00pm six days a week, closed Sunday, with the 90 minute limit when others are waiting and no price stated. A 9:00pm close is the latest stated finish for any first come court in Tallahassee, but the City does not write the word lights beside it, and lighting is not inferred here from a closing time.

Indoors, one court for two hours on a Friday lunchtime, Reserved Play only, at the City's table rate of $3.50 to $5.75 a session. That is a booked game for people who already have a four, not a session to join. Surface is not stated for either. The Friday window is the whole of the City's indoor statement about this centre: the other days read "No Pickleball".

faqs.q: Can I just turn up indoors?
faqs.a: No. The Friday indoor session is "Rerseve Play Only" in the City's spelling, and the City states that indoor courts have no first-come play. Ring 850-891-3940 to book.
Not stated for the outdoor courts, which carry no price. The indoor Reserved Play session costs $5.75 singles or $4.25 doubles, with senior rates from age 62.

slots.description:
Two outdoor pickleball courts with nets, "2 courts with net tie-downs", in the park that shares its grounds with the Sue Herndon McCollum Community Center. It is the one venue in Tallahassee where the City says you can borrow the kit: "paddles and balls available inside the Sue McCollum Community Center only during regular office hours". The courts are first come, first play only.

The centre's own page describes Lafayette Park as a 22-acre park with a recreation centre, an Arts and Crafts Center, a playground, a softball field, tennis courts, a picnic shelter and a one-mile trail. Its hours, the hours that govern the paddles, are Monday to Friday 9:00am to 9:00pm and Saturday 1:00pm to 9:00pm. The page states nothing for Sunday.
slots.getting_there:
501 Ingleside Drive, Tallahassee, FL 32303, as the City's pickleball page writes it, and the City writes it two ways. The Sue McCollum Community Center's page, for the building on the same grounds, prints "501 Ingleside Avenue", and the US Census address geocoder agrees with the centre, matching "501 INGLESIDE AVE, TALLAHASSEE, FL, 32303" at house-number level in Leon County inside Tallahassee city. OpenStreetMap holds no Ingleside Drive at that number, so there is one street here under two City spellings.

The City says nothing about parking. The centre's phone number is 850-891-3946.
slots.what_to_expect:
Two first come courts with nets, no session and no price, and a community centre beside them that lends paddles and balls during office hours. That makes this the one Tallahassee venue where arriving with nothing is a plan, provided you arrive between 9:00am and 9:00pm on a weekday or after 1:00pm on a Saturday. Outside those hours the courts are still there and the kit is not. The 90 minute limit applies when others are waiting.

No fee answer is published, because the City schedules neither Open Play nor Reserved Play here. Lighting is not stated and surface is not stated. For a rotation rather than a game, the City's free Open Play is at LeVerne Payne and Tom Brown.

faqs.a: Not stated. No Open Play is scheduled here and the City prices nothing for first-come play, so no fee answer is published.
The Sue McCollum centre is on the City's indoor schedule with Open Play on Wednesdays and Reserved Play on Monday and Friday mornings, but no indoor count is stated, so nothing indoor is published.

slots.description:
Three outdoor pickleball courts, and the one place in Tallahassee where the City says the courts can be used after dark. Its line reads "night play is available". The City's word is "night play", not "lighted", and that phrase is the whole basis of the lighting answer published here. It is the only lighting statement the City makes for any of its pickleball venues. The courts are first come, first play only.

The centre's own page says Walker-Ford opened on June 13, 1976, and gives hours of Monday to Saturday 9:00am to 9:00pm. The centre is on the City's indoor schedule with Open Play on Tuesday and Friday mornings 9:00am-1:00pm and Thursday evenings 7:00pm-8:30pm, but no indoor count is stated, so only the outdoor three publish.
slots.getting_there:
2301 Pasco Street, Tallahassee, FL 32310. The US Census address geocoder matched "2301 PASCO ST, TALLAHASSEE, FL, 32310" at house-number level, in Leon County inside the incorporated place Tallahassee city, and the centre's own contact block prints the same address and adds the postcode. That page also heads its hours block "2301 T-Pain Lane | 850-891-3970", the same number on a differently named street, and the Pasco Street spelling publishes because the pickleball page, the contact block and the Census all share it.

The City publishes nothing about parking or restrooms. The phone number is 850-891-3970.
slots.what_to_expect:
Three first come courts, usable at night on the City's word, and nothing else scheduled. Three courts is an odd number for pickleball: one game and a spare, or a rotation for a small group. The 90 minute limit applies when others are waiting, no price is stated, and surface is not stated.

The lighting answer is the reason to come, and it is worth being exact about. The City's phrase, "night play is available", is a statement about playing after dark rather than about lamps, and the courts are published as lit on that reading, with the phrase printed beside them. Nothing on the page says how late.

faqs.a: Not stated. The City says night play is available and gives no closing time for the outdoor courts. The centre building is open Monday to Saturday 9:00am-9:00pm.
Not stated. No Open Play is scheduled outdoors and the City prices nothing for first-come play, so no fee answer is published.
